headline: A 2020 executive order allows the U.S. to freeze the property of certain people connected to the International Criminal Court.
what_it_does: This order lets the U.S. government block, or freeze, property and interests in property belonging to certain people linked to the International Criminal Court (ICC), a court based in The Hague. Blocked property generally cannot be moved, sold, or used, and people in the U.S. are generally barred from dealing in it. The title does not say exactly which people are covered or why. Only the title was provided, so this summary is limited.

who_it_affects.group: Certain people associated with the International Criminal Court
who_it_affects.how: Property or assets they hold within U.S. reach could be frozen if they are named under the order.
They may be barred from handling or doing business involving property that is blocked under the order.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed June 11, 2020; the provided material does not state a separate effective date.
